name: Shopee Internal Report
tagline: Official-feeling internal deck for data-led business reviews and topic-based analysis readouts.
best_for: Internal Shopee decks that need either data-plus-conclusion pages or topic-analysis / decision-proposal pages under one consistent operating template.
avoid_for: Decks outside internal operating, reporting, strategy, diagnostic, or decision-making use cases.

path_rules: Run node scripts/shopee-template/package-deck.mjs outputs/<deck-slug>/index.html --single-file after writing or updating generated HTML.
Generated deck HTML must reference ./review-annotations.js for browser review comments.
Generated deck HTML must reference ./assets/brand/logos/shopee-logomark-no-text-square.png for the Shopee mark.
All deck-specific images, screenshots, and brand assets must live inside the output folder under ./assets/.
Single-file share copies inline deck-stage.js, review-annotations.js, and the Shopee mark.
delivery_packaging.portable_deliverable: Default to both: keep the folder package as the working copy and send index.single.html as the reviewer share copy.

visual_element_library.source_inspiration: Shopee internal samples plus red/blue analytical PPT patterns; raw source decks are not required at runtime.
semantic_color_rules: Red = critical risk or blocked status
Yellow = watchout, partial confidence, pending status
Blue = system, product, or automation capability
Green/Cyan = healthy, achieved, or improving status
visual_element_library.selection_rule: Choose elements by evidence shape after the slide-mapping-plan; do not copy source PPT page shapes unless their logic strengthens the business answer.

shared_visual_assets.use: Select one or two style anchors by content shape, then recreate the approved story with native HTML or PPTX elements.

input_modes.use_when: The user gives a natural-language internal report goal, rough bullets, partial data, or asks to generate the report structure from scratch.
input_modes.output: Infer the report spine, write business-answer hypotheses, mark missing data as assumptions or risks, then build the slide-mapping-plan.

input_modes.use_when: The user provides PPT, screenshots, pasted tables, or existing internal material and wants a smarter report distilled from it.
input_modes.output: Extract evidence, logic, owners, risks, and action asks; merge, split, or drop source pages based on business value before building the slide-mapping-plan.

data_pages.use_when: Need one topline table plus a short conclusion summary for leadership first-look pages.
Need one scope tracked across multiple periods, with trend commentary and watch points.
Need a dense grouped table plus numbered findings across multiple markets, cohorts, or segments.
Need many months or many markets in one rolling matrix, especially annual tracking.
Need two related tables on one page, usually topline status on top and benchmark/ranking below.
Need a breakdown table plus action cards, especially for lead-time, funnel-step, or process-stage optimization.

topic_pages.use_when: Need a decision page with background, constraints, options, and recommendation.

pre_generation_plan.user_confirmation_gate: Post the user-facing proposal plan (core conclusion, narrative line, one line per page) in chat and wait for approval before writing any deck HTML. Only skip if the user explicitly opts out.
pre_generation_plan.input_mode: natural-language brief first; PPT, notes, screenshots, and pasted data are supporting source material rather than conversion targets
intake_questions: What is the core conclusion the audience should remember?
Who is the audience, and what decision, alignment, or feedback do they need to provide?
Which narrative structure should the page or deck follow?
What does each screenshot, chart, or table represent, and what is the desired display order?
What should not appear, such as asks, CTAs, sensitive details, unfinished metrics, or extra next steps?
quality_rules: Every content slide needs a business-answer headline or hypothesis.
Body composition follows content shape; layout fragments are reference examples, not a mandatory menu.
Screenshots and charts are placed by asset role and business narrative order, not upload order.
Do not include asks, CTAs, or next-step panels unless the user requested them or the audience needs to act.
Missing information is recorded as assumptions or risks before HTML is filled.

split_workflow: Estimate normalized row count, column count, and density before filling the HTML table.
If any must_split_when threshold is met, duplicate the closest matching layout instead of shrinking below legibility.
Keep the same visual system and repeat the header, source note, and table definitions on each continuation slide.
Give every split slide its own business-answer headline and right-side finding/watch panel where the layout supports it.
Update agenda labels, data-sequence, footer page numbers, slide_count, and index.json after adding split pages.
do_not: Do not rely on browser auto-fit as the only solution for oversized source data.
Do not split purely by source page number when a business grouping is available.
Do not reduce dense table text below 8px.

layouts.best_for: Internal report cover with topic, team, and reporting period.
Agenda page introducing the chosen reporting scenario and section flow.
Topline data table plus short conclusion summary for leadership readouts.
Trend review page with one multi-period table and watch/action commentary.
Cross-market data detail page with numbered findings and supporting evidence.
Decision proposal page with background, option comparison, and recommended path.
Rolling dense matrix for annual plan tracking across markets and months.
Two related tables on one page, usually topline status on top and benchmark or ranking comparison below.
Breakdown table paired with specific improvement actions and quantified targets.
Closing page with presenter, team, and contact information.

steps: per-slide visual checklist on rendered PNGs, fix and re-shoot until clean
